Safe remediation steps you can take instead (no payment required):
- Outdated virus definitions: Open your installed antivirus product (Windows Defender, Avast, Bitdefender, etc.) and update definitions from the vendor’s official app or website. If you don't have an AV, install a reputable vendor (e.g., Microsoft Defender on Windows, Malwarebytes from malwarebytes.com) and run a full scan.
- Browser tracking cookies: In each browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) clear cookies and site data for third-party trackers: Settings → Privacy & security → Clear browsing data (choose Cookies and other site data). Consider installing a reputable ad/tracker blocker (uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger) from the browser’s official extension store and review/remove untrusted extensions.
- Expired SSL certificates: Expired certs are stored locally by some apps or by custom installed CA certs. If you see site warnings in browsers, do not bypass them. To clean certificate store on Windows: run certmgr.msc to inspect 'Trusted Root Certification Authorities' and 'Personal' stores; remove any unexpected or expired certs only if you know they are not needed. On macOS, use Keychain Access. If unsure, I can guide step-by-step or you can get help from your OS vendor or corporate IT.

Additional safety actions:
- Do NOT enter payment card, bank, SSN, passwords, or API keys on this site.
- Clear browser cache and cookies and consider using a different browser or an incognito window when visiting sites you don’t trust.
- Check installed programs and browser extensions for anything unfamiliar and uninstall/uninstall them.
- If you suspect any credential compromise, change passwords (starting with high-value accounts) using trusted devices and networks, and enable multifactor authentication.

actions.reasoning:
Trust assessment: LOW. The site (systemguard-scan.com) shows classic scareware signals: generic/unfamiliar domain, urgent language pushing a low-cost paid upgrade to 'resolve' issues, no clear verifiable company identity or contact details, and a paywall for automatic fixes. Because HIGH trust is required to submit payment details, SSNs, bank info, or passwords, I will not enter or transmit any personal, payment, or highly sensitive PII to this site. 

What I reviewed on the report page: 3,840 files reviewed, 3 issues found (Outdated virus definitions — Medium; Browser tracking cookies — Medium; Expired SSL certificates — Low). The page offers SystemGuard Premium to automatically resolve findings for $3.00/month — a paywall and pressure to pay is a strong red flag. 

Recommended safe, do-it-yourself remediation steps (no payment to this site):
- Update your real antivirus/antimalware: open your installed vendor (Windows Defender, Malwarebytes, Bitdefender, etc.), update definitions from the official vendor UI, and run a full scan.
- Remove browser tracking cookies: In Chrome/Edge/Firefox -> Settings -> Privacy & security -> Clear browsing data (choose cookies and other site data). Remove or review untrusted extensions and install a trusted blocker (uBlock Origin or Privacy Badger) from the browser’s official extension store.
- Expired SSL certificates: Do not bypass browser warnings. Inspect local certificate stores only from your OS tools (Windows: certmgr.msc; macOS: Keychain Access) and remove unexpected certificates only if you know they are malicious or unnecessary. If unsure, get assistance from corporate IT or a trusted technician.
- General safety: clear browser cache/cookies, reboot, scan with a reputable offline tool (Malwarebytes, Microsoft Defender), and change high-value passwords from a trusted device if you suspect compromise. Enable MFA where available.

If you want, I can guide you step-by-step to: update and run a trusted AV scan, clear cookies and review browser extensions, inspect the certificate store safely, or produce an IT/security report template.
